title: Lemon Pepper Chicken Wings
changes_from_base: Same baking-powder oven method as the Classic wings. Instead of the paprika rub, the wings are tossed in melted butter with lots of coarse black pepper, lemon zest and lemon juice.
summary: These wings use the same baking-powder oven method as the classic recipe, then get tossed in a fragrant melted butter with coarse black pepper, lemon zest and juice instead of a dry rub.
equipment: 2 wire racks that fit the trays

ingredients.item: chicken wings, split into drumettes and flats
fine sea salt or table salt
lemons, finely grated zest and 2 tbsp juice

steps.title: Dry and season
steps.text: Pat the split wings dry, then toss in a bowl with the baking powder, salt and pepper, following the same base method as the classic oven-baked wings. The baking powder raises the skin's pH so it blisters and browns well; stick to baking powder rather than bicarbonate of soda, which turns soapy.

steps.title: Arrange on racks
steps.text: Spread the wings skin-side up on wire racks over two trays, not touching each other. Refrigerating uncovered for 1 hour up to overnight dries the skin further for a crisper finish, though this is optional if you're short on time. About 20 minutes before baking, heat the oven to 120°C (100°C fan) with shelves in the lower-middle and upper-middle positions.

steps.title: Render at low heat
steps.text: Bake at 120°C (100°C fan) on the lower-middle shelves for 30 minutes to render the fat out gently. This slow stage means the skin isn't browning and drying out all at once later.

steps.title: Blast at high heat
steps.text: Turn the oven up to 220°C (200°C fan) and bake for 40-50 minutes more, swapping the trays halfway. Bake until deep golden, blistered and crackling, with the thickest drumette reading at least 74°C, ideally closer to 80°C for the most tender result.

steps.title: Make the lemon pepper butter
steps.text: Melt the butter in a small saucepan over low heat with the coarse black pepper and garlic powder, and cook for about 1 minute until fragrant. This brief cooking blooms the pepper's oils into the fat, giving a rounder flavour than sprinkling raw pepper on at the end. Take the pan off the heat and stir in the lemon zest and juice.

steps.title: Toss and finish
steps.text: Rest the wings for 5 minutes, then toss them in a big bowl with the warm lemon pepper butter until well coated. Scatter over the chopped parsley and a little flaky salt just before serving.

tips: Use freshly ground, coarse black pepper rather than a fine pre-ground tin - the fresh peppery kick is the whole point of this style.
Cook the pepper briefly in the butter before adding the lemon; it mellows and rounds out its bite.
Add the lemon juice off the heat, not while the butter is still cooking, so the sauce doesn't turn bitter or separate.
Toss the wings just before serving so the skin stays crackly rather than going limp in the sauce.
storage: Plain baked wings keep in the fridge for up to 3 days or freeze for 2 months; make the butter fresh each time rather than storing it sauced. Reheat wings in a hot oven until piping hot (74°C) before tossing in a freshly made batch of lemon pepper butter. Cool leftovers in a shallow container and refrigerate within 2 hours (within 1 hour on a day above 32°C).
